newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey in customs moves against money laundering.
newsitem.headline: Turkey in customs moves against money laundering.

text.p: Turkey is to tighten up its customs operations to counter cross-border money laundering after high-profile reports of two firms illegally importing gold and foreign currency, customs officials said.
They said the customs general directorate was preparing to send a directive to all customs posts aimed at clamping down on the illegal movement of goods.
In May, customs officials in Ankara seized in separate incidents 1.7 million marks and 24 kg (53 lb) of gold which representatives of two companies were seeking to bring into the country illegally.
Customs authorities were consulting with the Treasury undersecretariat and the central bank on new approaches to stopping money laundering, the officials said.
The Turkish parliament last November passed a law aimed at curbing money laundering as part of the country's fight against organised crime.
Progress towards implementation of the law, which envisaged the creation of an authority to investigate financial crimes, has been slow.
